title: How Refrigerators Evolved
upload_title: How Fridges Evolved ❄️ From Ice Houses to Your Kitchen #shorts #engineering

beats.text: Before fridges, fresh food spoiled in days.
Here's how keeping food cold evolved.
People salted meat and stored food in cool cellars, but summer heat still won.
Over 2,000 years ago, Persians built giant domed ice houses, called yakhchals, that kept winter ice frozen all summer.
In the 1800s, ice was cut from frozen lakes and delivered to homes, to cool a wooden icebox.
In 1834, Jacob Perkins built the first machine to make cold, by squeezing and expanding a gas.
Electric home fridges arrived in the 1910s, but early ones could leak toxic gas.
Safer Freon took over, until we learned it was eating the ozone layer.
Today's fridges use ozone-safe gases and a fraction of the power.
Follow to see how everything evolved.
